workload_fingerprint.zk_mode: Ligero HVZK masking: t_pad uniform coefficients (Z_H s_j) per row, 6D committed mask rows (prox/lin/quad x2/chain x2: q masked by a uniform zero-sum polynomial, AHIV22 u_add -- red team F1 fixed), evaluation on the coset g<w_n> disjoint from H (PROTOCOL.md 8b); malicious-verifier: HM96/GK step-0 commitment c_i = H(r_i || s_i) to both verifier coins before root, opened after root / after the test messages, prover aborts on a mismatched opening; challenges are functions of the coins alone (F2 fixed), simulator by rewinding with a CRH only (PROTOCOL.md 8c; redteam/simulator.py against the real verify()); NOTE: this statement publishes the operands a, b and the words y16 (statement_digest), so privacy is vacuous for it today -- the ZK claim is about the construction (masking + coins) and becomes meaningful once operands are committed (auth-integration LEAF_V2)

security.bound_model: interactive: statistical, live verifier coins committed at step 0 (HM96); no Fiat-Shamir loss
security.hash_assumption: collision resistance of Blake2b (coin commitments) + Blake3 (Merkle); the challenge expander is a PRG of the verifier's coins
security.zk_statement: malicious-verifier ZK (simulator by rewinding V* after step 0, CRH only); operands a, b and words y16 are PUBLIC in this statement, so privacy is vacuous today

backend.name: b-ligero chain, fp4-nvf4 relation (backends/direct/ligero/fp4)
backend.hints: torch on the prover's device, one CUDA graph per (system, l) (fp4/hints_device.py; bit-identical to numpy)

workload_fingerprint.preprocessing: constraint compilation (a function of NVFP4Params only, 0.20s)

instances.recipe: fp4-nvf4 synthetic (edge families random, zero-scales, subnormal-scales, top-scales, top-scales-zero-acc, span-scales, sparse, sparse-subnormal-acc, all-zero-codes, half-codes, max-codes, cancel, cancel-acc, mixed cycling per VU; model-recorded accumulators)

workload_fingerprint.omitted: external authentication; unopened columns hidden by Blake3 of a uniform column
workload_fingerprint.witness_generation: device hint generator (fp4/hints_device.py: the numpy lines as torch on the device, one CUDA graph) + fused CUDA witness kernel (witness_device.py; derived rows)
workload_fingerprint.note: 4096 VUs as 13 independently committed proofs of <= 341 VUs each (l = 8192 columns, 8 pad columns per proof); prover time = sum over the proofs; soundness = union bound; warm-up rep 0 = 13 untimed sub-batch(es); timed reps: 4 sub-batches in flight on their own streams (--pipeline; phase times = shares of the pass wall); public claim per VU = the final FP32 word, compared as three bit-field components (sign, exponent, fraction)

validation.checker: backends.direct.ligero.fp4.chain bench_vu_fp4 (verifier accepted every rep; prover self-check on the warm-up sub-batch; every dumped proof re-verified cold from its files by the Python file verifier)
validation.detail: 3 reps, 4096 VUs as 13 proofs at l=8192; dumps: 13/13 accepted cold from bytes

soundness.bound_model: interactive: statistical, live verifier coins committed at step 0 (HM96); no Fiat-Shamir loss
soundness.hash_assumption: collision resistance of Blake2b (coin commitments) + Blake3 (Merkle); the challenge expander is a PRG of the verifier's coins
soundness.zk_statement: malicious-verifier ZK (simulator by rewinding V* after step 0, CRH only); operands a, b and words y16 are PUBLIC in this statement, so privacy is vacuous today

privacy_terms_log2.mask_sampling_bias_per_symbol: 0 (rejection sampling; the simulator's distance is ChaCha20's PRF advantage on the mask key)

soundness.note: ZK: k = l + t_pad, every row carries t_pad > t uniform coefficients (Lemma 4.15); the linear test here sends nothing (the verifier encodes beta itself), so its query term is at most the Appendix-C ((k+l)/n)^t used; total_log2 is the union bound over n_proofs sub-batches; + the step-0 coin-commitment hiding term (commitment_hash)
